short: How much of a purchased ingredient survives to reach the plate.
seoTitle: Yield Percentage — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: Yield percentage is the usable portion of an ingredient after cleaning, trimming, peeling and cooking, expressed as a percentage of the purchased weight.
definition: Yield percentage is the usable portion of an ingredient after cleaning, trimming, peeling and cooking, expressed as a percentage of the purchased weight. A chicken bought whole yields far less than its billed weight in servable meat.
bodyHtml:
Why Yield Percentage matters

Costing at the purchase rate rather than the yielded rate understates every dish using that ingredient. On high-waste items such as fish, leafy vegetables and whole meats, the error is large.

Yield Percentage formula

Yield % = Usable weight ÷ Purchased weight × 100

True cost per usable kg = purchase rate ÷ yield %.

How Yield Percentage works in practice

Test yield once per ingredient per supplier: weigh in, prepare as usual, weigh out. Store the factor in the recipe sheet so all costings apply it automatically.

Worked example

Paneer bought at ₹360/kg with a 92% yield actually costs about ₹391 per usable kilogram.

faq.question: Which ingredients need yield testing most?
faq.answer: Anything trimmed, peeled or cooked down — meat, fish, leafy greens and whole spices.

faq.question: Does yield change by supplier?
faq.answer: Yes, noticeably. Yield testing is one of the fairest ways to compare two suppliers quoting different rates.
